question: The recap calls the Aether 'the Reality Stone'. The Dark World only says it is an Infinity Stone; the name 'Reality Stone' is first said in Avengers: Infinity War. Is naming the specific stone a spoiler at this point in the chapter?
options: Keep 'the Reality Stone'
Change to 'the Aether, an Infinity Stone,'
their_evidence: Mid-credits line in The Dark World: 'It's not wise to keep two Infinity Stones so close together.' The 'Reality Stone' name is spoken first in Infinity War ('the Reality Stone's been safely stored there with a man called the Collector').

entry.x: Jane Foster is infected with the Aether, an ancient weapon wanted by Malekith and his Dark Elves. They attack Asgard and kill Thor's mother, Frigga. Thor frees Loki to help him, and Loki seems to die saving his brother. Thor stops Malekith during the Convergence and turns down the throne, and the Aether, the Reality Stone, is handed to the Collector for safekeeping. On Asgard's throne, Odin is really Loki in disguise.

question: The recap says 'The orb holds the Power Stone'. In Guardians of the Galaxy it is only called an Infinity Stone; 'Power Stone' is first said in Avengers: Infinity War. Same question: keep the later name or use what this film says?
options: Keep 'the Power Stone'
Change to 'an Infinity Stone'
their_evidence: In the film Tivan opens the Orb, revealing an Infinity Stone; Ronan: 'now that I know it contains an Infinity Stone'. 'Power Stone' is first spoken by Thor in Infinity War.

entry.x: Peter Quill, taken from Earth as a boy the night his mother died, steals an orb that Ronan the Accuser wants for Thanos. He's arrested with Gamora, Thanos's adopted daughter, and bounty hunters Rocket and Groot, and they escape prison with Drax, who lost his family to Ronan. The orb holds the Power Stone. When Ronan tries to use it to destroy Xandar, the five hold the stone together and destroy him. Groot sacrifices himself and regrows as a sapling, and the five call themselves the Guardians of the Galaxy.

question: The recap says Frank is 'numbing himself with drugs and alcohol'. Neither plot summary mentions drugs or alcohol: he is shown haunted by hallucinations (Curtis Hoyle, Karen Page) and nearly takes his own life at his family's graves. Keep the phrase or change it?
options: Keep as is (if it is on screen)
Change to: 'Frank Castle has given up being the Punisher and is haunted by visions of his past.'
their_evidence: Wikipedia and MCU Fandom plot sections: Castle locks up his gear, is haunted by hallucinations, and puts a gun to his head at the cemetery; no drug or alcohol use described.

entry.x: Frank Castle has given up being the Punisher and is numbing himself with drugs and alcohol. Ma Gnucci, whose family he killed, puts a bounty on him, and when her crew attacks his building, Frank protects his neighbors and a coffee shop owner's family. At his daughter's grave, he tells her he isn't done yet, and goes back out as the Punisher.
